newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED FIRMER ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED FIRMER ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market edged higher in quiet trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the market started off with a shortage of Z$32.7 million and that Wednesday's maturities, amounting to Z$7.1 rmillion, would do very little to improve liquidity.
Hence, the Reserve Bank did not auction any treasury bills to mop up excess money on Wednesday morning, the dealers added.
But treasury bills were being sold on the secondary market at 20.5 percent, up from 20 percent the previous day while call money added one percentage point to 18 percent.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 22 percent from 20.75 and sold at 21.5 percent, up from 20 percent.
Bankers acceptances, which were quoted at 20.99 and 20.1 percent (buying and selling) on Tuesday, were at 20.75 and 20.25 percent.
